--- title: "Schedule & rosters" --- Most per-team endpoints key on a `team_id`. This guide shows how to discover a team id from the teams directory and then feed it into the schedule and roster loaders — all executed at build time. ## Discover a `team_id` ::: {#031c2717 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_teams teams = espn_mlb_teams() lookup = teams.select(["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_display_name"]) lookup.head(12) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Pick one team programmatically so the rest of the page stays in sync if ESPN re-orders the directory: ::: {#03a7d14d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl row = teams.filter(pl.col("team_abbreviation") == "LAD") team_id = row.select("team_id").row(0)[0] team_name = row.select("team_display_name").row(0)[0] print(f"Using {team_name} (team_id={team_id})") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Using Los Angeles Dodgers (team_id=19) ``` ::: ::: ## Team schedule ::: {#965aca91 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_team_schedule sched = espn_mlb_team_schedule(team_id=team_id, season=2024) # espn_*_team_schedule returns a tidy frame by default (return_parsed=True) print("schedule frame:", sched.shape) sched.columns[:16] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` schedule frame: (163, 15) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['id', 'date', 'name', 'short_name', 'time_valid', 'competitions', 'links', 'season_year', 'season_display_name', 'season_type_id', 'season_type_type', 'season_type_name', 'season_type_abbreviation', 'week_number', 'week_text'] ``` ::: ::: A few columns from the start of the season: ::: {#d80cd223 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} keep = [c for c in ["id", "date", "name", "short_name"] if c in sched.columns] sched.select(keep).head(8) if keep else sched.head(8) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Team roster Roster loaders return a tidy polars frame by default (`return_parsed=True`); pass `return_parsed=False` for the raw ESPN `Dict`. ::: {#dc851769 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_team_roster roster = espn_mlb_team_roster(team_id=team_id) print("roster frame:", roster.shape) roster.columns[:18] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` roster frame: (26, 60) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` ['position_group', 'id', 'uid', 'guid', 'first_name', 'last_name', 'full_name', 'display_name', 'short_name', 'weight', 'display_weight', 'height', 'display_height', 'age', 'date_of_birth', 'debut_year', 'links', 'slug'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#e92fb924 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} name_cols = [c for c in roster.columns if "name" in c.lower() or "position" in c.lower()][:5] roster.select(name_cols).head(10) if name_cols else roster.head(10) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip} The same `team_id` flows through *every* per-team endpoint for a league (`espn_mlb_team_record`, `espn_mlb_team_injuries`, `espn_mlb_team_leaders`, …), so once you have it you can compose a full team profile. ::: Next: [The parser layer](parsed-dataframes.qmd).
